assessments.reasoning: The Stanford imprint dates CS 110 to September 1969. Printed page 2 assigns distinct roles to the earlier Wirth and Hoare paper, the Stanford IBM 360 compiler based on it, and the implemented language described by the report.

The 1972 title and historical note corroborate continuity in language naming and distinguish the 16 January compiler issue. This separately dated revision cannot itself establish what the 1969 source records.

challenge.method: Compare the exact 1969 and 1972 Stanford title sheets and language descriptions against the Wirth–Hoare bibliographic record and the entire CHM entry. Test proposal, language, compiler, and revision interpretations.
challenge.results: The proposal based wording is explicit in the original Stanford description. The 1972 text marks a major revision and compiler version. The catalog lists multiple implementations and therefore supplies a bounded language crosswalk only.

limitations: The original report provides documentary authority for the distinction. The author bibliography and archive entry supply historical context.
